/-!
# Conjecture 10.62

by A. I. Sozutov

Construct an example of a (periodic) group without subgroups of index $2$ which is
generated by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product
of any two involutions from $X$ is odd.

The problem asks for an example, so it is formalised as the existence question
"does such a group exist?". The parenthetical "(periodic)" is an optional stronger
requirement and is stated as a separate variant.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G),
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      Subgroup.closure (conjugatesOf x) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ z ∈ conjugatesOf x, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Does there exist a group $G$ without subgroups of index $2$ which is generated by a
conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product of any two
involutions from $X$ is odd?

Here $X$ is the conjugacy class of an involution $x$ (an element of order $2$).
An element of infinite order has `orderOf` equal to `0`, which is not odd, so
`Odd (orderOf (y * z))` says that $yz$ has finite odd order.

claims.decomposer_note: Base form (parenthetical 'periodic' omitted): does there exist a group G with no subgroup of index 2 (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) generated by a conjugacy class X of some involution x (orderOf x = 2, X = {g x g⁻¹}, Subgroup.closure X = ⊤) such that for all x, y ∈ X the product x*y has finite odd order (in Lean `Odd (orderOf (x*y))` already forces finiteness since orderOf = 0 for infinite order, and x = y gives order 1 which is fine); X being a genuine conjugacy class of an involution rules out the trivial group, and by Glauberman's Z*-theorem any such G must be infinite and not locally finite, so 'construct an example' is an open existence question with expected answer yes, formalized as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), …` in the repo's question style.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful existence question; c08 chosen for the most direct encoding (`conjugatesOf x` for an `x` with `orderOf x = 2`, no redundant X variable), conjuncts in the order of the source text, and clear docstrings. Verified: `conjugatesOf x = {b | IsConj x b}` = {g x g⁻¹} via `isConj_iff`; `Subgroup.index = Nat.card (G ⧸ H)` so infinite index is 0 and `≠ 2` is exactly 'no index-2 subgroup'; `Odd (orderOf (y*z))` forces finite odd order because `orderOf = 0` for infinite order and `Odd 0` is false; `orderOf x = 2` rules out the trivial group. `Type` universe matches existing Kourovka files (1_74, 19_25).

claims.decomposer_note: The notebook's parenthetical marks an optional stronger requirement: the same existence statement with the additional hypothesis that G is periodic (every element has finite order, Mathlib's `Monoid.IsTorsion G`); this is a subordinate stronger form of the primary question (any periodic example is also an example of the base form), and it is the case of main interest for Sozutov since locally finite groups are excluded by the Z*-theorem argument.
claims.reviewer_why: Same statement with the added conjunct `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g), Mathlib's notion of a periodic group, matching the parenthetical stronger requirement. Equivalent across all candidates; c08 chosen for consistency with the base slot.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The split into a base form (parenthetical omitted) and a stronger periodic variant matches the notebook's text, and the notes' reading of each condition agrees with the Lean primitives used.

/-!
# Conjecture 10.62

by A. I. Sozutov

Construct an example of a (periodic) group without subgroups of index $2$ which is
generated by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product
of any two involutions from $X$ is odd.

The problem asks for an example, so it is formalised as the existence question
"does such a group exist?". The parenthetical "(periodic)" is an optional stronger
requirement and is stated as a separate variant.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.62»

/--
Does there exist a group $G$ without subgroups of index $2$ which is generated by a
conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product of any two
involutions from $X$ is odd?

Here $X$ is the conjugacy class of an involution $x$ (an element of order $2$).
An element of infinite order has `orderOf` equal to `0`, which is not odd, so
`Odd (orderOf (y * z))` says that $yz$ has finite odd order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G),
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      Subgroup.closure (conjugatesOf x) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ z ∈ conjugatesOf x, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a periodic group $G$ without subgroups of index $2$ which is generated
by a conjugacy class of involutions $X$ such that the order of the product of any two
involutions from $X$ is odd?

This is the stronger form indicated by the parenthetical "(periodic)" in the
problem: every element of $G$ is required to have finite order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.62».variants.periodic : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (x : G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      orderOf x = 2 ∧
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2) ∧
      Subgroup.closure (conjugatesOf x) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ z ∈ conjugatesOf x, Odd (orderOf (y * z)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.62»

items: 'Construct an example' is rendered as the yes/no existence question `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G …`, per the decomposition table and the repository's question idiom; `answer(True)` means such a group exists.

The conjugacy class X is encoded as `conjugatesOf x` for an element x with `orderOf x = 2`; this is the class of an involution, and all its members are involutions. Using `ConjClasses.carrier` instead would be equivalent but less transparent.

'The order of the product … is odd' is `Odd (orderOf (y * z))`; because Mathlib's `orderOf` returns 0 for elements of infinite order and `Odd 0` is false, this correctly requires finite odd order. For y = z the product is 1 with order 1 (odd), which is harmless and matches the informal statement.
'Without subgroups of index 2' is `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.index ≠ 2`; `Subgroup.index` is 0 for infinite-index subgroups so this never spuriously fires.
The group lives in `Type` (not `Type*`), following the existing Kourovka files (1_74, 1_40).
The periodic variant is a separate theorem `kourovka.«10.62».variants.periodic` that adds `Monoid.IsTorsion G`; the base slot omits the parenthetical, as the decomposition table prescribes.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted any slot and none raised decomposition objections. The candidates differ only stylistically in how the conjugacy class is encoded: `conjugatesOf x` (c04, c06, c07, c08), an existential `X = conjugatesOf x` or explicit `{y | ∃ g, y = g*x*g⁻¹}` (c01, c02), or `X : ConjClasses G` with `∀ x ∈ X.carrier, orderOf x = 2` (c03, c05); all are provably equivalent (conjugacy classes are nonempty and order is conjugation-invariant). Ambiguities in the source: 'any two involutions' could mean distinct, but x = y gives x*x = 1 of order 1 (odd), so the formalization is unaffected; 'odd order' is read as finite odd order, which the Lean `Odd (orderOf _)` enforces automatically. The group is quantified over `Type` following repository convention; this loses no generality for existence of a group with these (countably-closable) properties. c04's module docstring remark about Glauberman's Z*-theorem was left out to avoid commentary in the Lean file. Final file compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
